messages.subject: Altering the number of panels tabsetPanel at initialization
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to learn shiny, and I have a question about constructing a tabsetPanel based on information that's available at startup. In the example below I want to have 1 tab if twotabs is false and I want to have 2 tabs if two tabs is true. The false condition works fine, but the true condition just stacks the contents in the same tab and gives me some text rubbish (div tab-pane active Tab1 tab-5496-1) :)...

I believe I'm missing something simple. Can someone please point that out to me. Thanks.

twotabs = TRUE 

mytabs = tabPanel("Tab1",
           wellPanel(id = "PPanel", "This is tab 1"))

if(twotabs){
 mytabs = c(mytabs, tabPanel("Tab2", wellPanel(id = "PPanel", "This is tab 2")))
}

ui <- fluidPage(title = "tabset example",
        fluidRow(
          column(width=4, tabsetPanel(type="tabs", mytabs))))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
}
# 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

I believe I found a solution to my problem. And I thought I should post it here (I know how frustrating it is to look for a solution to a problem and find others asking the same question with no answers). This seems to do it for me:

Enter coderm(list=ls())
library(shiny)

TP1 = tabPanel("Tab1", wellPanel(id = "PPanel1", "This is tab 1"))
   TP2 = tabPanel("Tab2", wellPanel(id = "PPanel2", "This is tab 2"))

   output$mytabs = renderUI({
     twotabs = TRUE 
     #twotabs = FALSE
     if(twotabs == FALSE){
       tabsetPanel(type="tabs", TP1) }
     else{
       tabsetPanel(type="tabs", TP1, TP2) }
   })
